thread:
anya: Quick RFC follow-up: proposing an "activation-fence" pattern for air-gapped bundle upgrades. TL;DR: agent downloads & verifies bundle, stages files, runs per-component pre-activate hooks, but does NOT flip the active pointer until a nurse step (manual or timed auto-check) passes health criteria. This gives a deterministic rollback window without needing outbound comms.

mike_g: curious—what's the nurse step? manual button in the operator UI or an automated watcher?

anya: both. default is operator confirm via console/CLI; optional auto-confirm if all agent-local health checks pass within a configurable timeout (eg 5min). If health checks fail, agent reverts staged files to previous active snapshot.

rahul: how do we guarantee atomicity for mixed-component upgrades (runtime + agent + config)? we can't partially flip some components.

anya: plan is content-addressed snapshots per-release and an activation transaction log. agent writes an activation-record with: new-snapshot-hash, prereqs-hash, component-list. The active pointer flip is a single rename/symlink swap that the fs guarantees atomicity for. If agent crashes after writing activation-record but before swap, we detect on boot and either resume rollback or continue safe-commit.

sarah_platform: signing question: do we require the activation-record to be signed by customer KMS? offline customers will want HSM-backed signatures on activation metadata.

anya: yes — activation-record must be signed. Agent verifies signature before staging. For airgapped on-prem, signing happens at the operator workstation (customer tool) using their KMS/HSM. We include a simple verifier API so the operator tooling can produce a signed envelope.

mike_g: what about upgrades that change the agent binary? we need a bootstrap path so agent can self-upgrade without losing ability to rollback.

rahul: propose two-phase agent upgrade: stage new agent into parallel path /opt/redwood/agent.next, run a short self-check using a sandboxed runner, only then flip symlink. if flop, bootloader uses previous agent binary.

anya: exactly. also add a tiny native 'rollback executor' component that lives in the boot partition (minimal, signed) which can perform the swap if the new agent is non-responsive. That executor must be small and auditable.

mike_g: operator UX: CLI sample?

anya: sample command: `radmin activate --bundle sha256:abcd1234 --confirm` to confirm; `radmin activate --bundle sha256:abcd1234 --auto-watch 300` to auto-commit after 300s if checks good. rollback: `radmin rollback --to sha256:prevhash --force` (force requires operator key).

deploy-bot: deploy-log: activation-fence prototype pushed to branch activation-fence. CI build 452 passed unit + smoke.

ops-bot: note: we should add a default safe-timeout of 10m and an opt-in for unattended mode. Suggest exposing per-route health predicates (process liveness, kv-checks, port probes).

rahul: edge case: partial disk corruption while staging -> we should keep a verification pass that does block-level checksums before swap. list of checks: `sha256` compare, quick fsck on critical artifacts, verify migration scripts dry-run.

anya: agreed. I'll add a checklist in the RFC: verify signatures, verify checksums, run pre-activate hooks, run dry-run migrations, stage, run health probes, swap, post-activation probes, if fail -> rollback.

sarah_platform: don't forget audit logs: activation-record + operator signature + step timestamps must be appended to local audit log and optionally exported via USB for airgapped compliance.

mike_g: :thumbsup: this addresses a lot of the nonstop 'what if it dies mid-upgrade' questions. Can you add a diagram of activation vs apply paths to the RFC?

anya: on it. will add diagrams and a minimal sequence diagram + state machine. planning to iterate on the operator CLI UX next.

rahul: small nit — name the offline helper 'nurse' or 'watcher'? keep it consistent.

anya: calling it 'nurse' in the doc for now (nurse-agent = monitors local health & enforces rollback timer).

mike_g: thanks, will review the updated RFC when you push.

deploy-bot: note: thread pinned to #architecture for RFC review.
